parsed.explanation: Combined federal/state regime presents high risk. Federal entry screening can deny visas or impose permanent fraud bars for sex-document mismatch, reports of passport blocks/confiscation and allied advisories; nationwide government-funded facility exclusion plus many state/province bans and a documented bathroom arrest/trespass case. Immigration and prison custody harms are severe. Division public-accommodation and hate-crime protections help adult alone, but do not neutralise federal entry/facilities/custody. Adult-with-minor risk rises from age-targeted school, athletics, healthcare and criminal-teacher provisions. Absence of local violence is not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal visa/entry screening can refuse applicants when documents, records, or evidence cast doubt on sex; permanent lifetime immigration-fraud bars may follow. Existing X passports remain valid until expiry, but reports describe passports confiscated or blocked, and trans athletes for women’s sports are barred.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud bars are not automatic, require elements and limited waivers; litigation, legal-aid guidance, and some enjoined orders exist. Existing X passports remain valid.
entry_documents.interaction: A document discrepancy can move into secondary review, refusal, detention and possible bar; state/provincial IDs do not cancel federal screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented prison adoption of conversion-style rules, hair cutting, hormone removal; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. A bathroom arrest led handcuffing and 24h men’s ward placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National and state/provincial hate-crime statutes; lawsuits and court injunctions; no documented capital punishment for identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody can follow visa denial, facility refusal or arrest; federal/state enforcement can override local protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities by identity; many state/provinces ban congruent facilities, some criminalize them, and six states cover private settings. A capitol restroom arrest shows trespass enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has public-accommodation, housing and credit protections, hate-crime law, locality authority, a 2014 student-bathroom precedent and intended 2026 school reversal (unverified).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protections may reduce private/state accommodation friction, but federal facilities, government-funded spaces and border security remain national exposures.

care_services.exposure: Federal rules label minors’ gender care harmful, investigate schools and criminalize teachers facilitating social transition; records are subpoenaed; insurance and funding threats; 27 states/provinces restrict youth care.
care_services.protection: State prohibits providers from attempting to change minors’ gender identity; some national orders are blocked/enjoined; adult care not documented as protected.
care_services.interaction: A care or school encounter can generate documentation, disclosure or enforcement; a minor’s treatment can become investigated subject under federal/state rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official counterterrorism prioritizes violent secular groups hostile to the country, including radically pro-transgender ideology; national orders criminalize educators; state bathroom trespass arrests document enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Orders contested; some enjoined; official text claims no targeting for mere disagreement; national/state hate-crime and civil-rights statutes remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing supports exclusion and investigation; functioning enforcement of hostile rules is exposure, not recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Age-targeted school bathroom/pronoun restrictions, athletics bars, youth-care bans and criminal-teacher provisions can reach a trans minor; guardians may face questioning or enforcement if documents or support diverge.
minors_guardians.protection: State conversion-therapy ban, public-accommodation protections, 2014 bathroom precedent and risk assessment that youth rules unlikely extend to adults; same-sex family recognition exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor encounters can move from school/provider to records/police; guardian’s federal entry/facility risk remains; reversal and adult extension are uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No local trans violence rate documented, but police/custody harms include arrests, humiliation, birth-sex placement and abuse reports; allied advisories and supportive polls suggest social hostility.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State/provincial hate-crime and panic-defense repeal, civil-rights enforcement, national hate-crime statute; some courts hear complaints, but no visitor-facing remedy documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street response varies by state/province and officer; calling police may worsen exposure in detention-oriented jurisdictions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved practical state: passport/visa restrictions may apply or be litigated; school reversal unverified; map source missing; fraud bar discretionary; prison counts stopped; adult-extension conclusion is not judicial.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, ongoing suits, local hate-crime/civil-rights machinery and injunctions show contestable avenues.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcome depends on route, timing, state/province, minor status and whether federal or local authorities handle the encounter.

anchor_checks.comparison: Not as high as routine months of pretrial custody and coerced confessions for presentation, with no capital provision shown for visitors; however permanent immigration bars, custody abuse, facility enforcement and hostile official framing keep it near that tier.

Only superficially similar to ferry extortion and short detention: this regime is nationwide and legalized through facility/entry rules. Protective division law raises it slightly, but permanent bars and custody harm push it close to low 0.25.

Well below entry-refusal-only 0.35: refusal can become permanent ineligibility, and federal/state facility and custody measures add tier-1 exposures. Existing legal contest keeps it above severe-custody 0.20 but not near 0.35.
Far more severe than administrative secondary screening: documented criminal trespass enforcement, birth-sex custody and immigration-custody abuse place it well below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The operative experience is a federal hostile layer plus variable state/province layers. For an adult alone, the division’s public-accommodation and hate-crime statutes can improve private accommodation and some local reporting, but they do not offset border screening, government-funded facility exclusion, prison/immigration custody practices or nationwide document rules. The most severe path is document mismatch or facility use triggering investigation, refusal, arrest or detention, then birth-sex placement or reported abuse. For adults travelling with a minor, age-targeted school, athletics, records and care rules directly raise exposure and can drag the guardian into enforcement; local youth protections only partially counterbalance that. Thus the combined regime sits in high risk rather than elevated: severe but not execution/campaign level.
